overview: First year builds programming logic, computational thinking, engineering mathematics, and digital fundamentals. Focus on mastering one programming language (C or Python) thoroughly, writing clean code, and setting up your developer environment (Git, GitHub, VS Code, Linux basics).
keyGoals: Master foundational programming (Loops, Arrays, Functions, Pointers, Memory Management).
Build active GitHub profile with 3-5 clean repository projects.
Solve 50+ basic problem-solving and algorithmic logic questions.
Learn basic Git commands (init, add, commit, push, branch, pull request).
Explore Linux environment and terminal command line basics.

recommendedProjects.title: Student Record & Grade Management System
recommendedProjects.problemStatement: Educational institutes need a lightweight console tool to record student marks, calculate SGPA/CGPA, rank class toppers, and persist records across restarts.
keyFeatures: Create, read, update, and delete (CRUD) student records.
Automatic grade & GPA calculation based on university percentage thresholds.
Sorting by roll number or CGPA using custom sorting algorithms.
File persistence saving records to a `.dat` or `.csv` file.

recommendedProjects.title: Command-Line Bank Account & Transaction Tracker
recommendedProjects.problemStatement: Simulate core banking operations: account creation, PIN verification, deposits, withdrawals, and transaction ledger printing.
keyFeatures: Validation for minimum balance, negative inputs, and incorrect PIN attempts.
Mini-statement generating the last 5 transactions with timestamp.
Persistent ledger saved in structured text format.

recommendedProjects.title: Automated Personal Finance & Expense Tracker
recommendedProjects.problemStatement: College students struggle to manage monthly pocket money and track categorised expenses (Food, Books, Travel, Bills).
keyFeatures: CLI or lightweight GUI (Tkinter) to log daily expenses.
Category breakdown (pie chart or percentage summary table).
Monthly budget limit warning system (notifies when 80% budget is spent).
Export monthly summary report to CSV/Excel.

recommendedProjects.title: Personal Developer Portfolio & Resume Website
recommendedProjects.problemStatement: Every CSE student needs an online public presence showcasing their bio, projects, GitHub profile, and downloadable resume.
keyFeatures: Responsive design supporting mobile, tablet, and desktop screens.
Light/Dark mode toggle using JavaScript LocalStorage.
Interactive projects section linking directly to live demos and GitHub repositories.
Hosted live with custom domain or GitHub Pages URL.

recommendedProjects.title: Classic 2D Arcade Game (Snake / Tic-Tac-Toe with Minimax AI)
recommendedProjects.problemStatement: Implement game loop architecture, collision detection, score rendering, and an unbeatable AI opponent.
keyFeatures: Smooth 60 FPS game loop handling event polling, game state updates, and rendering.
High score leaderboard stored in local file.
Minimax decision algorithm for AI difficulty modes (Easy, Medium, Impossible).

hackathonFYStrategy.mindset: Treat 1st year hackathons as rapid learning laboratories. Do not worry about winning; focus on building a working MVP, meeting seniors, and learning Git collaboration.
hackathonFYStrategy.roleInTeam: FY students can handle frontend UI design, documentation/slide preparation, API testing, or user problem research.
hackathonFYStrategy.idealTeamComposition: 1 Senior (Backend/Architecture) + 1 Frontend Developer + 1 Logic/AI coder + 1 FY Student (Presentation/Testing/UI).

tasks: Install VS Code, GCC compiler, Python 3, and Git.
Create GitHub account, commit 'Hello World' and first 10 basic C programs.
Watch CodeWithHarry / Neso Academy C Introduction (Chapters 1 to 3).
Solve 30 practice problems on HackerRank / CodeChef in C.
Master pointer memory mechanics and write custom string manipulation functions.
Build Project 1: Student Record Management System.
Learn HTML5, CSS3, and basic JavaScript in 15 days.
Build and deploy personal Developer Portfolio to GitHub Pages.
Participate in first college internal hackathon or coding contest.
Build Project 3: Automated Personal Expense Tracker in Python.
Revise Engineering Mathematics & Digital Electronics question papers.
Review Git workflow: Branching, merging, and submitting Pull Requests.
